To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

participants in a CAM treatment for low back pain shifted from expectations about whether or not a therapy could relieve pain to expectations that included attention to broader lifestyle factors, long-term strategies to keep pain under control, quality of life, and wellness.
participants in this study shifted their treatment expectations over the course of the therapy from a focus on pain relief to a broader focus on self-care and long-term quality of living.
patients’ expectations about CAM therapies for chronic low back conditions change over time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how expectations change over time in the course of CAM therapies.
the relationship between expectations and outcomes of CAM therapies.
the relationship between patients’ expectations about a treatment, and the outcomes of the treatment, particularly for Complimentary and Alternative Medicine (CAMS) therapies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the findings of this study support the notion that the shift in treatment expectations of patients with chronic low-back pain seeking CAM therapies to greater acceptance of the chronicity of pain and the importance of self-care is a positive outcome of CAM therapies.
the findings of this study support the need for further exploration of patient expectations of CAM therapies, including the development of a validated questionnaire to assess these expectations.

the shift in treatment expectations over the course of CAM therapies for chronic low back patients may be a positive outcome of CAM treatment, and that CAM practitioners should capitalize on this shift to encourage feelings of control rather than disappointment surrounding this realization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CAM therapies are more than a treatment for pain; rather they are an approach to wellness.
patients who seek CAM therapies for chronic pain are more likely to be accepting of the chronicity of pain than those seeking conventional care.

CAM treatments are effective for pain relief and that the treatments are effective for improving quality of life and well-being, and for increasing awareness of the need to take personal responsibility for health.
The main takeaway from our work is that
patients’ expectations of treatment change over time, particularly with regard to acceptance of pain as a chronic condition.
patients’ expectations of treatment change over the course of CAM treatment and this change should be considered in the design of future research.
the relationship between patient expectations and treatment outcomes is complex and may be influenced by the nature of the treatment and how it is presented to the patient.
